## 7. ADE20K Pretraining Overlap Determination

SegFormer-B1 (nvidia/segformer-b1-finetuned-ade-512-512) was pretrained on the ADE20K *training* split (20,210 images). Fine-tuning images are drawn from that SAME training split, so they were already seen during pretraining. The Golden Test Set, validation tuning set, and benchmark set are all drawn from the ADE20K *validation* split, which the pretrained checkpoint never observed. Therefore the pilot measures in-distribution continued training on seen data, NOT independent generalization to a novel domain. Generalization can only be claimed on the validation-split-derived evaluation sets.

| Partition | From ADE20K training split (seen by pretrained checkpoint) | From ADE20K validation split (unseen) |
|---|---|---|
| Fine-tuning train (1%) | 48 | 0 |
| Golden Test (200) | 0 | 200 |
| Validation tuning (50) | 0 | 50 |
| Benchmark (50) | 0 | 50 |

## 8. Conclusion

All data-isolation checks **PASS**. The Golden Test Set is strictly disjoint from the benchmark, validation tuning, and fine-tuning partitions. No evaluation image is reused for training, hyperparameter selection, threshold tuning, or early stopping.

However, because the fine-tuning images originate from the ADE20K **training** split — the exact corpus used to pretrain `nvidia/segformer-b1-finetuned-ade-512-512` — the pilot does **not** measure independent domain generalization. It measures continued/refreshed training on data the checkpoint has already optimized against. Generalization claims are restricted to the validation-split-derived Golden Test, validation tuning, and benchmark sets, which the pretrained checkpoint never observed.
